description: We are a family-based team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge. We are passionate about space exploration, science, technology, and artificial intelligence.
summary:
Lost No More: Voyage Beyond is an interactive web platform that transforms NASA's scientific and historical information about forgotten explorers into an educational adventure for children ages 6–12.

Children are naturally curious and eager to explore, but traditional scientific and historical resources can be technical or difficult for them to understand. Inspired by our family's shared passion for STEM education and our differing generational perspectives, we created a storytelling-based voyage to the Moon and Mars, where a chatbot named PIP guides children through an immersive space adventure.

With this approach, children can explore different missions and interact with PIP and spacecraft through storytelling. The explorers are introduced through explanations of who they are, why they were sent into space, how their equipment works, and what they discovered. Children learn not only what these missions accomplished but also how they operated and why their discoveries matter to humanity. The platform allows children to ask questions after the visit, with answers generated using NASA-provided data and resources. At the end, children receive a scrapbook containing summaries of each of the explorers. 

Our goal is to inspire curiosity about science, technology, engineering, and space exploration while helping children recognize that every mission has a story worth remembering.
details:
Lost No More: Voyage Beyond is an interactive web platform that transforms NASA's scientific and historical information into an interactive space adventure. Children travel virtually to the Moon and Mars, meet six explorers, interact with PIP (an AI-powered chatbot), ask questions, and explore their missions through storytelling.

Instead of simply reading facts about space missions, children can have conversations with NASA's robotic explorers, learning about their discoveries, challenges, and achievements through personalized storytelling. It makes complex space science easier and more enjoyable for children ages 6-12.

The project is intended to inspire children's curiosity about space exploration and STEM while introducing them to NASA's remarkable missions and ensuring these explorers' stories are not forgotten.

As a team, we brainstormed and discussed how to create an engaging storytelling experience for children. Considering today's visual learning approaches and children's educational needs, we developed the idea of a platform that makes children feel as if they have actually traveled to the explorers' locations, seen them in their environments, and experienced their missions. Rather than simply reading information, children become part of the journey.

We considered children's ages, learning abilities, visual learning approaches, ease of use, scientific accuracy, and interactive storytelling. AI tools were used to help transform NASA-provided data into child-friendly content and assist with platform design. However, the original ideas, creative direction, storytelling approach, and workflows were developed through our team's brainstorming and discussions. AI supported the development process; it did not create the concept.

Web Interface

The project is an interactive 3D educational web application built with JavaScript, Three.js, HTML5, CSS3 and Vite, integrating an Azure-hosted AI-powered RAG chatbot with voice narration to help children explore the stories of NASA's spacecraft and robotic explorers.

Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning

We organized the information into approximately 130 searchable text chunks and indexed them using Azure AI Search and OpenAI embeddings. Through Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), our application retrieves relevant NASA information before generating conversational responses.

The project uses publicly available scientific and historical information from NASA and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL). Our dataset focuses on six explorers: Opportunity, Spirit, InSight, Ingenuity, the Apollo Lunar Module, and the Lunar Roving Vehicle.

1. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

We use RAG to connect generative AI with information collected from NASA sources. When a user asks a question, the application searches its NASA knowledge base for relevant information before generating an answer. This approach helps reduce AI hallucinations and keeps responses grounded in mission-related evidence.

2. Large Language Models (LLMs)

We use Azure OpenAI's GPT-4.1 mini model to generate natural, conversational answers based on the retrieved NASA information. The AI responds from the perspective of the selected explorer, creating a first-person storytelling experience. For example, users can ask Ingenuity why it stopped flying on Mars or ask Opportunity about its scientific discoveries. The model is instructed to use retrieved evidence rather than invent unsupported mission details.

3. AI-Powered Semantic Search

We use OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small model to convert NASA knowledge and user questions into numerical vector representations. Azure AI Search combines vector similarity with keyword-based retrieval to identify relevant information. Our retrieval system also filters information by the selected explorer, helping ensure that answers are based on the correct mission.

4. AI-Powered Voice Narration

We integrate Azure AI Speech to convert AI-generated answers into spoken narration. Users can read the answer, listen to the narration, and explore the supporting NASA sources.

5. Responsible and Evidence-Based AI

We designed the project to prioritize factual accuracy and transparency. The application retrieves relevant NASA information, generates answers using that context, and provides source references so users can explore the original material.
